feedback:
Approve this single-variable test. The candidate is the iteration 8 design (score 431.1, best raced so far: y 0.065 m, base_speed 1.2, kp 2.6, kd 0.6, ki 0.1, span x -0.07 to 0.07, sensor_size 0.016) with kd changed from 0.6 to 0.5. Everything else is unchanged, and the geometry and controller values are all in range.

The evidence supports this step. Iteration 9 (base_speed 1.1, score 425.1) left the oval at 20/20 with mean 951. Its s-bend and slalom still ended 20/20 off track, with s-bend max_error 0.0626 and slalom max_error 0.0655 (iteration 8 gave 0.0622 and 0.0654 at base_speed 1.2). Speed is therefore not the limiting factor, and lowering it cost about 6 points. My iteration 9 rule now points to kd 0.5 at y 0.065 with base_speed 1.2. Iteration 4 (kd 0.45) and iteration 5 (kd 0.6) showed that kd moves oscillation in opposite directions on the oval and s-bend, so this is a fair test of whether the s-bend overshoot is damping-limited. Iteration 5 to 8 also showed that the geometry levers (y 0.03 and sensor_size 0.012) lowered the score, so y 0.065 and sensor_size 0.016 are held.

Risks: the kd drop may raise oval and slalom oscillation, which was 0.178 and 0.222 at kd 0.6 and y 0.065. Line-loss events at y 0.065 are already high (0.65 on the oval, 1.0 on the slalom), so I do not expect the s-bend to gain finishes from this change alone. Two iterations remain after this one, so the race is worth more than another reading-only round.

Next race, read the results as follows. If the oval stays at 20/20 and s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 or finishes appear, keep kd 0.5 and treat it as the new reference. If the score falls below 431 with oval oscillation above 0.2, return kd to 0.6 at base_speed 1.2 and y 0.065, which is the iteration 8 design. If the s-bend is still off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at kd 0.5, the next lever is kp, not speed.
requested_changes: Keep base_speed 1.2, y 0.065, kp 2.6 and sensor_size 0.016, and set kd to 0.5. Iteration 9 (base_speed 1.1) showed speed is not the limit on the s-bend (max_error 0.0626), and iteration 4 at kd 0.45 versus iteration 5 at kd 0.6 showed kd shifts oscillation on the oval and s-bend.
If the score falls below 431 at kd 0.5 with oval steering_oscillation above 0.2, return kd to 0.6 at base_speed 1.2 and y 0.065, which is the iteration 8 design (score 431.1, the best raced).

If the s-bend is still off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at kd 0.5, test kp 2.8 at kd 0.6. Iteration 3 to 4 (kp 3.0 to 2.6) changed s-bend max_error only from 0.0625 to 0.0617, so kp is a weak lever and this should be the last test before the final iteration.
